text.p: Tropical Storm Beth is currently in the South China Sea, moving to the west southwest about 12 mph. Beth has top winds near 50 mph but is weakening and will continue to do so as it begins to dissipate during the next 36-48 hours off the eastern coast of south central Vietnam. There is still some risk to shipping off the Vietnam coast, but this threat will gradually diminish. Later in the period, moisture from the dissipating tropical cyclone will likely bring a period of heavy rain to Vietnam, where more flooding will occur from the seemingly endless string of storms and rain this season.

Tropical Cyclone Antoinette is in the southwestern Indian Ocean, well east northeast of Madagascar at this time, moving to the west southwest around 18 mph. Top winds, currently near 70 mph, are weakening and will drop to under 40 mph by the 48 hour period. At that time, the storm should be a few hundred miles north of Mauritius Island and still a few hundred miles east of the coast of Madagascar. Antoinette remains a threat to shipping, but not to land.

Hurricane Lili is currently about 155 miles south of Bermuda, passing south of the island on a northeast track at 25 mph. Lili has top winds of 90 mph and will continue to weaken as it loses tropical characteristics during the next 24-36 hours. Lili is a threat to shipping only.

A major storm system has produced heavy rainfall and flooding from New Jersey to southern New England through Sunday afternoon. This storm is not associated with Lili to the south. Heavy rain continue in parts of southern and central New England where rivers may rise above flood level through Monday. Conditions will improve by Tuesday as the storm weakens.
